question: A provision appears under a Guidance heading and uses the word 'should.' Is it mandatory, and when may a deviation be appropriate?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No — a provision under a Guidance heading is a recommendation, not a mandate. Guidance statements describe recommended practice in typical situations, typically using the verb "should," and deviations are allowed when engineering judgment or an engineering study indicates the deviation is appropriate. Only Standard statements (using "shall") are mandatory. Standards (mandatory): - "Guidance—a statement of recommended practice in typical situations, with deviations allowed if engineering judgment or engineering study (see Section 1D.03) indicates the deviation to be appropriate. All Guidance statements are labeled, and the text appears in unbold italic type. The verb 'should' is typically used. The verbs 'shall' and 'may' are not used in Guidance statements. Guidance statements are sometimes modified by Option statements." - By contrast, "Standard—a statement of required, mandatory, or specifically prohibitive practice regarding a traffic control device," for which "the verb 'shall' is typically used." Guidance (recommended): - Typical examples of Guidance "should" statements include: "guide signs should be limited to no more than three lines of destinations," and preferential-lane guide signs on conventional roads, "if used, they should comply with the provisions for guide signs in Chapter 2D and any principles… that engineering judgment finds to be appropriate for the conditions" — both are recommendations subject to engineering judgment, not requirements. Support (context on deviations): - Section 1D.03 explains that the application of engineering study and engineering judgment is a fundamental principle of the use of traffic control devices; even for Standards, in limited site-specific cases a documented engineering study may support a deviation — for Guidance, the threshold is lower (engineering judgment or engineering study suffices). - Section 6P.01 notes that, except for notes clearly classified by headings, the information in typical applications "can generally be regarded as Guidance" — i.e., recommended rather than mandatory. Visual evidence: [Image 4] Table 2C-6 illustrates the normative gradation directly, distinguishing "Optional," "Recommended," and "Required" uses of the Advisory Speed plaque. [Image 5] shows Guidance statements in unbold italic type using "should" (e.g., signal-face positioning recommendations) alongside bold Standard text, illustrating the labeling convention. [Image 7] shows a Guidance statement in italic type using "should" for SCHOOL word-marking letter height. [Image 8] shows a typical-application notes page where Standard, Guidance, and Option headings clearly separate mandatory "shall" statements from recommended "should" statements. Citations: - Section 1C.01 Standard §1 (p.13) - Section 1D.03 Support §2 (p.32) - Section 6P.01 Support §2 (p.857) - Section 2D.06 Guidance §2 (p.209) - Section 2G.10 Guidance §2 (p.420) - Table 2C-6 (p.196) - Page 54 - Page 971 - Page 859
gold_answer: It is recommended practice, not a mandatory Standard. A deviation may be appropriate when engineering judgment or an engineering study indicates that the deviation is suitable for the specific situation.
